<reason>PRO built a clean externality frame (the seller keeps the money, twenty-six neighbours carry the risk) and then relentlessly turned CON's own reform examples into evidence for the motion: every "correction" was externally forced and every one ended, shrank, or struck down the program. CON's best move was the residency/citizenship distinction in Q2, but PRO answered it directly (on-ramp to a passport, Schengen permit, property route inflating housing) with proper A1/A2 structure. CON then conceded citizenship-by-investment is "a small, already-dying subset," effectively giving away half the motion, and never answered the lawful-oligarch gap beyond generic sanctions law, which PRO correctly noted cannot entry-ban a Union citizen. CON's "convergence means nothing left to abolish" turn was clever, but PRO's closing landed the decisive point that convergence deletes the property purchase, which was the very revenue and housing fund CON kept invoking; CON's closing did not answer this. PRO's clipped first rebuttal is a minor execution cost but does not change the outcome.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Rebuttal 1 reframing of CON's Cyprus/Malta/Portugal examples—"three examples of reform working are three examples of the motion happening"—combined with the closing observation that CON's reformed model strips out the property purchase that generated the revenue CON defended, left CON defending only "the transaction itself."</best_rebuttal>
